newsitem.title: USA: GCA Jan. coffee stock data seen mainly neutral.
newsitem.headline: GCA Jan. coffee stock data seen mainly neutral.

text.p: New York coffee futures are likely to be unimpressed by monthly inventory data released late Tuesday showing a modest increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks, traders and analysts said.
Supplies of green coffee stored in U.S. warehouses rose in January by 15,000 60-kg bags, to 1,264,000 bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported.

"It is a neutral number," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "There was some Mexican coffee coming in, but the fact is there is still not a lot of coffee showing up at a time when there should be."

The port of Laredo, Texas, a major receiving point for coffee imported from Mexico, posted the largest gain in coffee stocks. Laredo stocks rose by 44,000 bags to 217,000 bags, the GCA said. Inventories increased by 30,000 bags, to 163,000 bags in Jacksonville.
But warehouse stocks in New Orleans and New York declined in January. New Orleans stockpiles fell by 25,000 bags to 465,000 bags and New York inventories decreased by 20,000 bags, to 87,000 bags.
U.S. inventories still lagged well behind year-ago levels. U.S. stocks reached 2,151,000 bags in January 1996, while the January 1995 cache totaled 4,076,000 bags.

But the historical comparisons are not likely to prompt any panic buying, traders said, noting the future market's rapid 50 percent increase since the start of the year based on diminished availability.
"The market is just ignoring the stocks," one trader said, "because people are assuming there will be no material change to build coffee supplies."
